# Skills use `open_start_run`; README documents agent buttons and adding a tool

## What to build

Teach the bundled skills about graph-manager's new agent tool, and document the feature for users and graph-execution developers.

1. `to-tasks` skill: at its final step, when the tool `open_start_run` (MCP server `graph-manager`) is available to the agent, call it with the task folder and the spec after the folder validates and is committed, and tell the user the Start run form is open in graph-manager; otherwise keep today's ending (show the command and offer `run-graph`).
2. `run-graph` skill: in a graph-manager terminal, when the user asks to start a run and `open_start_run` is available, call it instead of running the CLI, unless the user asked to start the run without them (or asked for a suite, `--resume`, or `--sandbox`), in which case run the CLI as today.
3. `apps/graph-manager/README.md`: document the agent buttons, the `open_start_run` tool, and a "Adding a tool" section for graph-execution developers.

Facts to write (from the spec `docs/prd/agent-tools.md`, which you should read in full):
- The Terminals page has buttons **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **OpenCode**, **Qwen Code**, plus **Plain terminal** (`Ctrl Space n`). An agent button opens a terminal in the chosen workspace, connects graph-manager's tools, then runs the agent inside the shell (quitting it leaves a shell). A CLI that is not installed has its button disabled.
- How each agent is connected: Claude Code `--mcp-config <dataDir>/agents/claude-mcp.json --allowedTools mcp__graph-manager`; Codex `-c mcp_servers.graph-manager.command="graph-manager-mcp"`; OpenCode the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var; Qwen Code has no flag or env var for this, so graph-manager writes `mcpServers["graph-manager"] = { "command": "graph-manager-mcp", "trust": true }` into the workspace's `.qwen/settings.json` and commits only that file (`chore: connect graph-manager tools for Qwen Code`), once; it refuses (409, no terminal) when that file has uncommitted changes, a merge/rebase/cherry-pick is in progress, or HEAD is detached. Nothing is pushed.
- `graph-manager-mcp` is a stdio MCP server on the terminals' `PATH` (`<dataDir>/bin/graph-manager-mcp` → `dist/server/mcp.js`); it reaches graph-manager with the per-boot `GM_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, `GM_INTERNAL_URL` and the terminal's `GM_TERMINAL_ID`, so it works only inside graph-manager terminals (outside, it lists no tools). Not on Windows (no shim there).
- `open_start_run { tasksDir, spec, provider?, options? }` opens the Start run popup prefilled in the browser tab that shows the calling terminal; other tabs get a toast `<Agent> in <repo> wants to start a run` with **Open**. It returns right away; the user reviews and clicks Start run. Paths may be relative to the agent's cwd or the workspace root and must be inside the workspace.
- Adding a tool (developers of graph-execution, not end users): create `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/<name>.ts` exporting `defineTool({ name, description, input: z.object({…}), async run(input, { ctx, terminal, workspace, cwd }) { return { text, isError? } } })`, append it to `TOOLS` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/index.ts`, add a test next to it, rebuild (`npm run build -w graph-manager`) and restart. Every agent sees it with no config change, since `graph-manager-mcp` fetches the list from `GET /api/internal/tools`. A tool that needs the browser queues a request on `ctx.agentRequests` (see `open-start-run.ts`).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `docs/prd/agent-tools.md` — the whole spec.
- `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` — the bundled skill; the final paragraphs after "### 6. Validate the task files (REQUIRED)" are where the new ending goes.
- `packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` — the bundled skill; see the "In a graph-manager terminal (`GM_INTERNAL_URL` is set)" bullet (around lines 36–41) for the existing graph-manager wording to sit next to.
- `.claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` — this repo's own copies, currently identical to the bundled ones; apply the same edits so they stay identical. (`.agents/skills/*` are older copies; leave them alone.)
- `packages/graph-execution/src/install/skills.test.ts` (lines 100–125) — content assertions on the bundled skills that must keep passing; add assertions that `to-tasks` and `run-graph` contain `open_start_run`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/skills.ts` — graph-manager copies the bundled skills into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` at startup, so agents in its terminals get these edits.
- `apps/graph-manager/README.md` — sections `## First steps` (line ~64), `## The app` (line ~137, with `### Reviewers`, `### Keyboard`), `## Local development` (line ~175), `## Limitations` (line ~195). Add `### Agents and tools` under "The app" and `### Adding a tool` under "Local development"; mention in "Limitations" that agent tools need the POSIX shim (not on Windows) and that agent requests are kept in memory only.

## Patterns to follow

**Skill wording** — keep the skills' plain, imperative style. Suggested to-tasks ending (adapt to fit):
```md
Finally, start the run or hand it to the user:

- **In graph-manager** (the tool `open_start_run` from the `graph-manager` MCP server is in your tools): commit the task folder and the spec, then call `open_start_run` with `tasksDir` (the task folder) and `spec` (the PRD file). It opens graph-manager's Start run form for the user, prefilled. Tell the user it is open and that they can review the options and click **Start run**. Do not start the run yourself.
- **Elsewhere:** tell the user the tasks are ready, show the command, and ask whether to start it now. …(existing text)…
```
Keep every string the tests assert (`.agents/tasks/<id>.json`, `validate-tasks.mjs .agents/tasks`, `--web`, `**3**`, `**2**`, `Do not sleep, poll`, `graph-execution open`, frontmatter).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (identical)
### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (identical)
### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/install/skills.test.ts` — assert `open_start_run` appears in both.
### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/README.md` — the sections above.

- **VALIDATE**: `diff packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md .claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md && diff packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md .claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` prints nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both bundled skills (and the `.claude/skills` copies) mention `open_start_run`, say when to use it, and keep the old behaviour outside graph-manager.
- [ ] `apps/graph-manager/README.md` documents the agent buttons, how each agent is connected (including the Qwen commit), `open_start_run`, and "Adding a tool".
- [ ] `npm test -w graph-execution -- src/install/skills` passes.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- src/install/skills
```
